SM.nonempty_fibres covers BOTH printed conclusions. The first conjunct quantifies over every pair of integers n,r without an admissibility or existence premise, and states precisely n >= 3, 2*abs(r) < n, and (n,r) != (3,0). HasGenericPolygonRotation asserts existence of an actual member of genericFibre on GenericPolygon, the cyclic quotient of actual G1/G2 generic labelled tuples. It witnesses a natural vertex count m whose integer cast equals n and explicitly requires 3 <= m. The redundant NeZero witness follows from that inequality. Negative or too-small integer n therefore cannot exploit vacuous raw Generic predicates on short tuples; the at-least-three condition comes from the source polygon domain. genericFibre_nonempty_iff proves the quotient/representative correspondence using Quotient.exists_rep and polygonProjection. genericPolygonRotation is the genuine quotient lift of the finite principal-turn sum divided by 2*pi, justified by cyclic invariance; the fibre is its actual level set at the real cast of r, not a definition restating admissibility.

Necessity uses actual Generic-to-Regular inclusion, the strict rotation bound and nonzero rotation of the SAME regular triangle. Sufficiency covers all integer constructors: zero forces n >= 4; positive k uses a regular seed with 2*k+1 vertices; negative -(k+1) uses actual reversal of the positive k+1 seed and proved regularity/rotation reversal laws. The complex seed really has vertices q^i.val, with q = exp(i*2*pi*k/(2*k+1)). The closing edge and corner are included through q^m = 1, every edge is nonzero, and the principal argument is proved to equal the actual angle in (0,pi), without assuming an unwrapped argument. Its actual finite sum has rotation k. The zero seed is the printed bowtie; actual vector identities and principal-angle swap/negation prove four-turn cancellation and regularity. No seed genericity is assumed. Distinctness of every seed vertex and the bowtie's explicit individual angle values are unnecessary intermediate claims: the theorem needs a Regular seed with the exact rotation, which the code proves directly. Repeated actual strict-interior insertion gives every larger vertex count, retaining Regular and rotation via the reviewed insertion geometry and sum theorem. It does not replace insertion by a supplied angle inventory or require Generic. A different choice of repeated subdivision edges is harmless for this existence conclusion; this review does not claim that the implementation proves the proof paragraph's particular one-edge construction.

Regular perturbation establishes openness of the complete Regular domain, including positive collinearity and zero turns. It proves continuity of the actual ambient rotation sum using the genuine complex-argument slit domain. Continuity plus proved integer values yields a neighborhood on which rotation is equal, and full density supplies an actual Generic tuple there. This is a proved alternative to the source's convex-ball/path argument, with no desired local existence or regularity result supplied as a target premise.

The second conjunct quantifies over every natural n >= 3 and every actual nonempty open subset U of LabelledTuple n, with its ordinary finite product topology on real coordinate pairs, and produces P in U satisfying the full original Generic predicate. All ordered triples of pairwise distinct vertex indices occur in determinant avoidance, not only triples containing a consecutive pair. The area polynomial is evaluated on the actual affine tuple line; its nonzero witness assigns (0,0),(1,0),(0,1) to those three distinct vertices. For every pairwise remote edge triple the code proves its six endpoint indices distinct, independently assigns the source witness endpoint pairs and computes -1 for the actual 3-by-3 determinant of the homogeneous line rows. Repeated coordinates in that witness show only nonvanishing somewhere in the full tuple space, not Generic or membership in U. Actual segment points satisfy their line equations, and a common point of three segments forces the determinant to vanish. Only the required sufficient condition excluding concurrence is used, not an unjustified converse.

Polynomial avoidance is proved using restrictions to genuine affine tuple lines and the finite root bound for a nonzero real univariate polynomial. A global nonzero witness makes the line polynomial nonzero at parameter 1; continuity gives a nonempty open preimage of U around parameter 0. The finite intersection of the resulting dense open nonvanishing sets is dense, including the empty remote-triple family. This sound alternative to one multivariate product establishes simultaneous avoidance in arbitrary U. G1 alone forces any three distinct edge interiors sharing a point to be pairwise remote, via the reviewed actual adjacent-segment geometry. Remote determinant exclusion therefore establishes full G2. There is no guarded weaker genericity, oracle crossing relation, assumed generic perturbation, literature axiom or strengthened target premise.

The Lean type is a conjunction of exactly the two printed clauses. (1) Existence: source says for integers n,r a generic polygon with n vertices and rotation r exists iff n>=3, 2|r|<n, (n,r)!=(3,0). Lean: forall n r : Z, HasGenericPolygonRotation n r <-> 3 <= n /\ 2*|r| < n /\ (n,r) != (3,0), with HasGenericPolygonRotation (Fibres.lean 20-22) = exists m : N, NeZero m, 3 <= m, (m:Z)=n, (genericFibre r).Nonempty. genericFibre (Admissible.lean 28-29) is the level set {Q | genericPolygonRotation Q = (r:R)} in GenericPolygon m, the quotient of {P : LabelledTuple m // Generic P} by the cyclic shift (Chambers.lean 14-21), and genericPolygonRotation is the Quotient.lift of rotationNumber (Admissible.lean 18-23) -- this is the source's fibre U_{n,r} on the orbit space of def:polygon (source line 27-35), and nonemptiness of the quotient fibre is equivalent to existence of a generic labelled representative with rotation r. rotationNumber P = (sum_i principalTurn P i)/(2 pi) (RotationNumber.lean 10-11), principalTurn P i = arg(conj(edge P (i-1)) * edge P i) (RegularLocus.lean 15-16, RegularPairs.lean 54, EuclideanPlane.lean 55) with Re = <u,v> and Im = det(u,v) (EuclideanPlane.lean 57, 61), hence exactly def:regular's principal turn in (-pi,pi) with cos = <u,v>/(|u||v|) and sign = sgn det (source lines 386-394) and lem:rot's rot(P) (line 408). Genericity: Generic = G1 /\ G2 (Generic.lean 11-19), G1 = chi P i j k != 0 for pairwise distinct i,j,k with chi = sign det(P j - P i, P k - P i) (Chirotope.lean 10-11), G2 = no point in three distinct edgeInterior's with edgeInterior the open-parameter segment (Polygon.lean 57-58); this is verbatim def:generic (source lines 100-108) and the lemma's own gloss 'every determinant of three distinct vertices is nonzero and no three distinct edge interiors meet'. The explicit 3 <= m inside the existence predicate encodes def:polygon's 'Let n >= 3' (source line 28): the source has no polygons with fewer than three vertices, and without the clause the raw Generic predicate is vacuous on 1- and 2-tuples (no pairwise-distinct triples), which would falsify the iff at e.g. (n,r)=(1,0); so the clause is the source's domain restriction, not an added hypothesis on the theorem. Domain of quantification is the full integer plane for both n and r, as printed. (2) Density: source says for n >= 3 every nonempty open set of labelled n-tuples in (R^2)^n contains a generic polygon. Lean: forall n : N, 3 <= n -> forall U : Set (LabelledTuple n), IsOpen U -> U.Nonempty -> exists P in U, Generic P, where LabelledTuple n = ZMod n -> R x R (Polygon.lean 14) carries Mathlib's product topology (no custom TopologicalSpace instance anywhere in SM/), i.e. the standard topology on (R^2)^n. Exact match. Both clauses are non-vacuous, hypotheses and conclusions coincide with the printed ones, and nothing is stronger or weaker. The prior review (work/reviews/lem-fibres.json, read only after forming this judgement) reaches the same verdict and records the SM12->SM15 excerpt as byte-identical; I concur.
